summary: Index external-grant admission by principal and exclude revoked or effectively expired history before claim hydration

replay.detail: No claim rewrite, projection replay or history removal. The SQL expiry filter uses the latest policy, retains missing-fields validation candidates, and preserves legacy absent-principal ChatGPT grants.

schema.detail: Schema-on-open adds claims_assistant_v1_principal_index on claims(kind, COALESCE(json_extract(body,'$.fields.principal'),'assistant/chatgpt')). This additive derived access path changes neither STORAGE_VERSION (20), RULES_VERSION (26), the registry nor shared projection digests. Existing supported stores install the index automatically; subsequent opens reuse it.

rules.detail: Profile admission, grant lifecycle, approval-once consumption, issuer checks and retention semantics are unchanged. Multiple same-profile grants remain allowed; service issuance remains disabled.

compatibility.detail: On a 16-core x86_64 benchmark host (32 threads, Linux), real bound daemon APIs with bearer authentication and one concurrent pairing completion per GET were measured against exact baseline 98e550cb75. With 10000 expired grants per principal and 200 samples per mode, approval-once GET p95 improved from 965.184401 ms to 54.153648 ms; caller-bound-allow improved from 933.049170 ms to 46.173346 ms. Both indexed modes pass q39 <=100 ms. These are in-process production routers over Unix/TCP sockets, not an external daemon-process startup benchmark. SQL work still scales with matching principal history; the index avoids unrelated principals and inactive records no longer hydrate into Rust. Subscription deferral counts explicitly retain their request-history seek, avoiding a generic subject/kind history scan under SQLite's default estimates.

downtime.detail: The first store open missing the index waits synchronously for its construction. Exact index CREATE DDL on a synthetic 1000000-claim real Store schema took 1524.850241 ms (about 1.525 s) on a 16-core x86_64 benchmark host (32 threads, Linux 6.18.51). This is one measurement on that host, not a guaranteed rate of 1.5 seconds per million rows or a startup-time guarantee. Main database size grew from 1421651968 to 1481170944 bytes. This measures index-build startup work only, not complete restart-to-API time or cold-disk startup; allow additional first-open delay according to local history and hardware. Later opens do not rebuild the index.

manual.detail: No operator SQL, data conversion, credential reissue or manual migration is required. Allow the first open to finish index construction.

recovery.detail: Claims and signed bodies are unchanged. A binary rollback leaves the index in place: previous binaries can ignore it, and SQLite keeps maintaining it on writes. An interrupted first-open index build can be completed by normal subsequent schema-on-open installation; no history deletion or repair SQL is needed.
